title: Cato Agr.135.1-3
author: Ancient
content:
11. Cato On Farming, 135.1-3

Buy tunics, togas, cloaks and blankets, and clogs at Rome. Hoods and
ironware (scythes, spades, mattocks, axes, harness, and chains) at Cales
and Minturnae, spades at Venafrum. Carts and sledges at Suessa and in Lucania.
At Rome and in Alba, vats and basins; rooftiles made in Venafrum. Rome-made
plows are good for heavy soil, Campania's for dark soil. Rome's yokes are
the best. Detachable plowshares will do the best. Oil mills at Pompeii
and in Nola at the shop of Rufrius. Rome for nails and locks, hooks, oil
vats, water pitchers, and wine jugs, in fact all sorts of bronze, in Capua
and Nola. Capua's Campanian baskets are good; at Capua also ropes for hoists
and all kinds of cordage.
